conversations.title: Chicago’s 23rd Disability Pride Parade celebrates visibility and inclusion
conversations.reply: Love seeing events like this, it's amazing to have a space where people can be themselves without apology. The fact it's been running for 23 years is a testament to the community's strength.

conversations.title: ICC Sydney opens accredited Quiet Room for accessibility, wellbeing
conversations.reply: This is exactly the kind of thing that makes a difference, having a quiet space can be a game-changer for people with sensory issues.

conversations.title: ADA celebration highlights new accessible trails in Lindley Park
conversations.reply: It's fantastic to see new accessible trails being developed, and celebrating them as part of an ADA event is a great way to promote inclusion.

conversations.title: City's key role in helping disabled people hailed
conversations.reply: It's great to see cities taking steps to support their disabled residents, these small changes can make a huge difference to people's daily lives.

conversations.title: Stairlift Grants: How to Get a Disabled Facilities Grant for a Stairlift
conversations.reply: It's the everyday things, like being able to get around your own home, that really matter to people's independence and quality of life. Simple changes can have a big impact on daily life.

conversations.title: Berlin Pride Event Cut Short After Car Hits Crowds
conversations.reply: This is just terrible, Pride events are supposed to be a celebration of love and acceptance, it's heartbreaking to see it end in violence.

conversations.title: Samantha Renke
conversations.reply: Samantha Renke is doing amazing work, her advocacy is making a real difference and it's great to see her voice being heard.

conversations.title: All by Samantha Renke | Metro UK
conversations.reply: Samantha Renke's writing is a breath of fresh air, she's a talented journalist and a passionate advocate for disability rights.

target_reply: Hey Samantha, I'm a big fan of your work and it's fantastic to see you speaking out on issues that matter to our community, your voice is really valued.
funding: Check out the Disabled Facilities Grant for stairlifts and other adaptations at https://www.1stchoicestairlifts.com/resources/stairlift-grants-disabled-facilities-grant, and don't forget to look into UnLtd (unltd.org.uk) and Access to Work (gov.uk) for more support and resources.
moment: It's Disability Pride Month, and I'm celebrating by embracing my own identity and amplifying the voices of disabled people around me. Let's keep pushing for a world that's more inclusive, more accessible, and more proud of its diversity ,  and let's start with the small, everyday things that can make a big difference.
target: Samantha Renke (UK wheelchair user, actress, The Lifestyle Pod)
